declarations.description:
Rows × columns of checkboxes or radio buttons in one form control: the permissions of GitHub and Okta (resources ×
read, write, admin), notification preferences (events × email, push, SMS) or a survey's agreement scale.

With `type="checkbox"` each row takes any number of columns; with `type="radio"` exactly one, and the arrow keys move
along the row. `toggles` adds tri-state checkboxes that check or clear a whole row, a whole column, or a column within
a group of rows (rows that share a `group` are listed under a header row). A disabled row or column keeps its
choices and is skipped by the toggles. With `type="radio"`, `use-all` puts a "Use all" button under each column
title, which chooses that column in every row.

A cell can hold content beside its control, which also names the control: text from `cells`
(`{"email":{"a":"ada@example.com"}}`) or anything `renderCell` draws. That is how a cell shows the value it stands
for, as a merge of duplicate records does (`c2-record-merge`).

Under a row, a line across the matrix can hold a comment field, a note or a photo: put an element in the row's slot,
`detail-<row value>` (`<c2-textarea slot="detail-q1">`), or set `renderRowDetail`. A row with neither has no line.

`value` maps each row's `value` to the checked columns' values (a string for radio rows). Under a `name`, a form
receives one `name[row]=column` entry per choice. `required` asks for at least one choice, or for every row to be
answered with `type="radio"`. The control takes part in `c2-form-field`, which names and describes it.

Each choice is named by its row and column, and the matrix is a table: a screen reader reads the column title as it
moves along a row. On a narrow screen the table scrolls sideways with its first column held in place.

declarations.description:
Rows × columns of typed inputs in one form control, with totals: sizes by colour quantities, hours per person and
day, SLA targets per priority and channel, a survey's grid of numbers.

Each column's `type` says what its cells take: `number`, `duration` (stored in minutes, typed `1:30`, `1h 30m` or
`90`), `date`, `time`, `text`, or `select` with its `options`; `cell-type` is the type of the columns that name none.
Numbers are read and written in the page's language. `totals` adds a column with each row's total, a row with each
column's total, or both with the grand total where they meet; only `number` and `duration` columns are summed.

The keys travel like a sheet: Enter moves down (Shift+Enter up), the up and down arrows move between rows in a text
cell, and left and right move between columns once the caret is at the edge. Pasting cells copied from a sheet
(tab-separated) fills the cells from the one pasted into, one change for all of them.

`value` maps each row's `value` to its cells by column value (`{"s":{"red":4}}`); an empty cell has no key. Under a
`name`, a form receives one `name[row][column]=value` entry per value. A number outside its column's `min` or `max`,
or text that is not a value of its column, makes the matrix invalid; `required` asks for at least one value. Rows and
columns are those of `c2-choice-matrix`: groups, descriptions and disabled rows or columns work the same way.
declarations.name: InputMatrix

declarations.description:
Two or three duplicate records side by side, one row per field, to pick the value each field keeps, as the duplicate
merge of a CRM reads. Each record is a column whose cells show its values; choosing a cell picks that record's value
for the field, and "Use all" under a column takes every field from that record.

`records` are `{ id, label, values }`. `fields` (`{ key, label, group, description }`) list the rows in order; left
out, every key of the records is a row. Every field starts on the `primary` record (the first by default), so the
merge only asks for what changes; a field still on it by default follows a change of `primary`. `merged` is the surviving record: the primary's values with each field taken from
the record chosen for it. `preview` adds a column with the result of each field. `value` is a `c2-choice-matrix`
value, the record id chosen for each field key, and a form receives `name[field]=record` for each (a key holding `[`
or `]` nests in a server that parses brackets, so keep field keys plain).

Everything `c2-choice-matrix` with `type="radio"` does applies: the arrow keys move along a field's row, a disabled
field keeps the primary's value, and `required` asks for every field to be chosen.

declarations.description:
A rated form: criteria in categories, each answered on a scale, weighted, and totalled as you go, as an interview
scorecard, a support QA review or a supplier evaluation reads. Some criteria are critical: a failing answer there
fails the whole card, whatever the total.

Rows are the criteria (`{ value, label, group, weight, critical }`), columns the points of the scale (`{ value,
label, points, na, fail }`): `1` to `5`, strong no to strong yes, pass and fail, with an optional "not applicable"
column that leaves a row out of the total. A column earns its `points`, else its value read as a number, else its
position. Each row's score shows in a column after the scale, each group's subtotal on its header, and the total,
the percentage and the verdict of `bands` under the card. `score` is the same at any time, and `score-change` fires
with it when the user answers.

Everything `c2-choice-matrix` with `type="radio"` does applies: a comment under a criterion goes in its
`detail-<row>` slot, cells can show what a level means (`cells`: a rubric), `use-all` answers every criterion at once,
and `required` asks for every criterion. A criterion takes one answer whatever `type` says, and a disabled one counts
towards nothing.
